newsitem.title: UK: European bourses fall on new inflation fears.
newsitem.headline: European bourses fall on new inflation fears.

text.p: European stocks fell sharply on Thursday as jittery markets saw a surprising decline in U.S. unemployment claims as signs of renewed inflationary pressure and higher interest rates.

The dollar was little changed from late Wednesday's levels with foreign exchange traders preferring to wait for Friday's U.S. retail sales and producer price data for pointers on interest rate prospects.
London and Paris made hefty losses as the drop in U.S. weekly jobless claims prompted selling in the bond market and a and a 0.4 percent drop in Wall Street at its opening.
London's fall of 0.7 percent followed a sharp decline on Wednesday which ended a four-day run of record closes.
"Really this is doing our market some good and should bring it back to a more sensible level," one trader said.

London's recent bull run and a surge in other European bourses have been fuelled by signs the U.S. economy, after rapid expansion, is slowing to a level where it can sustain inflation-free growth and low interest rates.
Any change in this scenario would be regarded as bad news by markets. Hence investors were worried about the U.S. jobless figures and Friday's American wholesale inflation data for September.

Markets on both sides of the Atlantic were alarmed by the U.S. figures showing the number of Americans signing up for first-time state unemployment benefits fell last week by 22,000. Markets had expected an increase.
The report rekindled jitters about wage-driven inflation, dealt a big blow to the bond market and sent the Dow Jones Industrials down to 5904.9 points from a close of 5930.62.
The ripples were felt in Europe. In Paris, stocks were down by 0.8 percent after the U.S. data but also weighed down by a bout of profit-taking.

But traders said the fall was in line with weakness in bonds, London stocks and other European centres and there was no cause for concern for Paris, which should continue to climb after a short-term correction.

Frankfurt floor trade, which closed before the U.S. figures, ended down nearly one percent, depressed by overnight losses on Wall Street and weaker government bonds, which slipped after the Bundesbank left interest rates unchanged.
"We're seeing a bit of caution with Wall Street down," said one trader.

The dollar edged down against the yen but strengthened slightly against the mark after the Bundesbank, as expected, held interest rates. Some traders saw worries over Yeltsin's health as helping the U.S. currency.
"The dollar market was well bid. This underlines the sensitivity of the market because of the current situation in Russia," said Jeremy Hawkins, senior economic adviser at BankAmerica in London.
The dollar had a brief and temporary overnight surge in Asia after unfounded rumours of Yeltsin's death circulated in the market.
But trading was quiet and forex dealers said they expected the current levels to remain at least until Friday's U.S. data.
"There is not much that will rock the market until the end of the week," said BankAmerica's Hawkins.
CURRENCIES AT 1430 GMT
The dollar was at 1.5297 marks and 111.18 yen compared with 1.5287 marks and 111.55 yen late in Europe on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1430 GMT
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was down 21 points at 3988.3.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was down 15.10 at 2,131.61.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt closed down 22.24 at 2680.75.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed at $381.75 an ounce in the afternoon compared with Wednesday's close of $381.45. Silver was seven cents stronger at $5.01.
